hotspots.title: Adorni scandal deepens
hotspots.blurb: Manuel Adorni, former Chief of Staff to Argentine President Javier Milei, resigned amid allegations of illicit enrichment and misuse of public funds. Multiple officials testified about unauthorized purchases made using government credit cards, sparking an internal investigation and judicial probe.
hotspots.affect: This scandal commands disproportionate attention due to its moral charge and the high-profile nature of Adorni's role, which was central to Milei's administration. The allegations of corruption and nepotism directly contradict Milei's anti-establishment rhetoric, creating a crisis of credibility.

hotspots.title: Vox blocks Andalusian investiture
hotspots.blurb: Vox, Spain's far-right party, rejected Juanma Moreno's bid for re-election as Andalusian president in the first investiture vote, demanding policy concessions. The standoff risks triggering new elections in October if no agreement is reached within 48 hours.
hotspots.affect: This hotspot commands attention due to its high-stakes political brinkmanship, with Vox leveraging its kingmaker role to push its nationalist agenda. The potential for new elections amplifies the sense of urgency and polarization.
